scene.title: One query. A careful mixture.
scene.description: Follow q·k/√2 through a mask, subtract-max softmax, and a weighted sum. Try a +1000 common shift: the result stays the same. “No keys” deliberately leaves the row undefined.

nodes.text: Animation reveals a fixed computation. Bar lengths encode probabilities, never confidence in a fact.

cues.text: Read q=[a,1], three key vectors, and scalar values [2,−1,4]. Scores include the same optional shift.
Exclude masked keys from the maximum and denominator. Subtract the maximum allowed score before exponentiating.
The bars reveal exp(score−max) divided by the allowed-key sum. Shifting all scores does not change these ratios.
Multiply each probability by its value, then sum. No allowed keys means undefined; zero bars are not a valid distribution.

accessibility.text: One attention row uses q=[a,1], keys [1,0], [0,1], [−1,1], values [2,−1,4], and score dot(q,k)/√2 plus a common shift. Exclude masked keys; compute m=max of allowed scores, p=exp(score−m)/sum exp(score−m). The output is 2p1−p2+4p3. A common shift changes neither p nor O. With no allowed keys the row is undefined; the zero bars are placeholders, not a successful normalized row. Animation reveals this fixed calculation; it does not train parameters.

scene.title: Many small journeys. One update.
scene.description: Scrub a three-stage fill/drain schedule. F and B label forward and backward work; μ1, μ2, μ3 identify microbatches. Their sizes are 1, 2, 1. The toy scalar objective uses four examples, so divide the accumulated gradient sum by four, not by three.

nodes.text: Four examples · microbatch sizes 1, 2, 1 · same old parameters until every gradient returns

children.text: Idealized equal-duration steps. A diagram of ordering, not a throughput forecast.

cues.text: Start with an empty gradient accumulator. All forward and backward work in this batch uses the same old w.
Forward work drains toward stage 3. Empty cells are scheduling bubbles, not completed work.
Backward starts at stage 3 in reverse microbatch order. A downstream result is not yet a returned stage-1 gradient.
μ3 has returned to stage 1: one example. Its gradient sum is available, but no optimizer update is allowed.
μ2 adds two examples. Three of four are back. Still no update.
μ1 completes the four-example batch. Divide the total gradient sum by four and commit one simultaneous scalar update.

accessibility.text: Idealized three-stage fill/drain schedule: forward F(j,s) occurs in slot j+s, backward B(j,s) in slot 9−j−s, for zero-based microbatch j and stage s. Each slot lasts one illustrated second; this is not a hardware speed prediction. Examples (x,y) are μ1:[(1,2)], μ2:[(2,0),(1,1)], μ3:[(−1,3)]. Loss per example is (wx−y)²/2. Gradient sums are w−2, 5w−1, w+3; batch gradient is their sum divided by four. All use the old w. Stage-1 gradients return at 8, 9, 10 seconds in μ3, μ2, μ1 order; update once at 10 seconds to w−rate×mean. At w=1 and rate=.1, sums are −1,4,4, mean 1.75, new w .825. Averaging microbatch means would be a different objective.

scene.title: Move the tile. Keep the sum.
scene.description: A 2×2 tile computes part of C=A×B from 3×3 inputs. Change the row or column tile to expose an edge. Scrub through two loads, three k-products, and one final store. PAD cells are explicit zeros, never out-of-range reads.

nodes.text: C = A × B · 3×3 matrices · a 2×2 output tile · FP32 traffic model
Scratch tiles reuse loaded values. Padded zeros never issue a global read or an out-of-range write.
Traffic counts scalar loads + stores for this tile only. They do not predict device bandwidth or speed.
Accumulators update after k=0, then k=1, then k=2. Write C once after all three products.

cues.text: Choose a 2×2 output tile. A is [[1,2,0],[−1,3,1],[2,1,4]] and B is [[2,1,−1],[0,3,2],[1,−2,1]]. All accumulators begin at zero.
The first k tile is loaded. Valid global reads are counted; the same scratch values serve several output products.
Accumulate the product for k=0. Keep these partial sums; C is not written yet.
Add k=1. Loading the next tile must not reset the accumulators.
The second k tile contains k=2 and padding. PAD contributes zero without a global read.
Add k=2. Edge output cells stay outside; they are never written.
Write each valid output once. This idealized traffic model ignores cache hits and hardware transactions, so it is not a speed claim.

accessibility.text: Compute a selected 2×2 output tile of a 3×3 matrix multiplication. A=[[1,2,0],[−1,3,1],[2,1,4]], B=[[2,1,−1],[0,3,2],[1,−2,1]]. C=[[2,7,3],[−1,6,8],[8,−3,4]]. The first scratch load covers k=0,1; the second covers k=2 plus padded zero. Add products at 1.5, 2.4 and 4.4 seconds; write at 5 seconds. If the output tile has R valid rows and C valid columns, input reads total 3R+3C, stores RC, and FP32 traffic is 4(3R+3C+RC) bytes. The naive no-cache input count is 6RC. These count scalar global operations for one output tile, not actual memory transactions or measured throughput. Padding never reads or writes outside a matrix.
